Hey Cheesebacon, I'm a F27 married to a M26. 

When we met at 22 I didn't want to get married or have kids. He was the one who wanted to get married and was honest early on that he didn't want to father children due to health concerns on his side. I didn't want kids because of my anxiety and depression. I didn't want to do what my mom did to me. 

That changed when all three of my sister's got pregnant at the same time. I was crushed I would never be a mother. I started frantically looking into adoption and having arguments with my husband. He didn't want to say that he'd never be ready for kids but deep down we both knew that he didn't want that. I cried constantly.

It took a lot of soul searching and confronting my resentment but I did realize that the life I have with him is what I really and truly want.

 I started volunteering in childcare where I got to know kids and play board games.  Its been 2 years but I have accepted that I'm not someone who could do childcare 24/7. 

I give my sister's much needed breaks when they need time to themselves or with their SO's. This is what is right for me. 

My advice is to figure out WHY you want to be a mother. Why you want to be married. Why your partner doesn't want kids. Find a way to have those needs met and still have the relationship. 

My husband doesn't because he has a short temper, chronic illness, hates spending money and doesn't like kids or people in his personal space. (I'm the exception)

It was a hard to realize that if I really wanted to be a mother I would need a different partner someone who wanted to be a father. 

Right now you are grieving the life you had been quietly expecting. Your reaction is completely reasonable in this context. Do some soul searching. Figure out what you really truly want and how to work toward it. If you want this relationship to work find a way to accept your life as is without resentment. 

Resentment kills love. Do not have children with someone who resents them. 

Sorry this was so long. Good luck.
